correctness.rationale: Each equivalence block contributes either its size or zero to the boundary, independently of other blocks, yielding the exact product. For b≥2 the ratio rho_b=(1-q_b)/q_b is strictly positive. After dividing factors of lower degree, coefficient z^b is precisely m_b rho_b; hence all non-singleton multiplicities are uniquely and constructively recovered. The singleton invisibility, fixed-n completion, low-degree sharpness example, and abstract rough-lattice product follow by explicit arguments. Direct exact-rational checks of all partition shapes up to nine points and three sampling biases succeeded. Infinite correctness relies on proofs rather than enumeration.

value.rationale: The inverse problem is naturally motivated by whether one can recover unknown equivalence-granulation sizes from a scalar boundary-size observation law rather than inspect or label all blocks. The theorem completely characterizes identifiability, gives an exact finite inverse algorithm and sharp singleton and low-degree obstructions, and demonstrates that the distribution is finer than the canonical unweighted rough-set lattice. It is not merely a finite enumeration, a renaming or arbitrary size restriction.
